stances_toward.note: Viv Ansanm, formed in September 2023 by G9 and G-Pèp, was created to attack the Haitian government (police stations, government buildings, infrastructure) and to fight the international force (Wikipedia, tier 4). Adversary is our reading, not a source's word, and it is the rare grade by design: the sources show hostile attacks on the state, not a stated aim of replacing it, so if a stricter reading is taken this becomes rival. Bond none: no kinship or affinity is named. Trend stable: the 2026 coverage shows continued killings, with no sign of a turn. Trend moved to cooling on 29 October 2026 on the events of 18-21 October: gangs attacked the force in Croix-des-Bouquets and left four Salvadoran technicians missing, which El Salvador says the gangs hold (AP, 21 Oct); the mission's envoy told the Security Council that the gangs were testing the force, with reprisal killings and advances into Kenscoff and the Artibonite (AP, 19 Oct). Cooling here means the hostility is hardening; the grade stays adversary.

stances_toward.note: Our reading (confidence C), added 2026-10-29 after the ambush of 18 October. The grade rests on the government's own words as AP reported them: Bukele announced a rescue operation on 21 October and warned the gangs of a harsher response, and on 22 October told the gangs, as AP quoted him, "we can finish with you too", after saying the crackdown had already finished them at home. A declared aim of the other side's defeat is the test for adversary. Trend cooling: the hostage-taking escalated the conflict. Bond grievance, dated from the hostage-taking; no older wound was found in the sources read. Bukele did not name the group holding the men, so the grade covers the Haitian gang coalition as the counterpart until a holder is confirmed.

relations_from.summary: Armed gang members ambushed Salvadoran Air Force personnel serving with the Gang Suppression Force in Port-au-Prince with gunfire and explosives; four Salvadoran service members were missing after escaping their burning armoured vehicle.

sources.title: Four Salvadoran air force members missing after gang ambush in Haiti

relations_from.summary: Gangs ambushed a Salvadoran Air Force armoured vehicle on 18 Oct and took four Salvadoran technicians, attached to the international Gang Suppression Force, hostage. The portal reports it on 21 Oct.

sources.title: Reuters: El Salvador says Haiti gangs hold four Force members hostage

relations_to.summary: Salvadoran special forces deployed to Haiti on 22 October to find the four men held by gangs, after Bukele warned on 21 October that the gangs would face a harsher response if they were not freed alive and unharmed (AP). The sources read to 27 October report neither a release nor a confirmed death, and do not name the group holding the men.
